commitResults.messageTitle: Leave GUI code out of Codecov coverage reports
commitResults.messageBody:
GUI classes are not covered by automated tests in this project, as CI
runs without a display. Codecov therefore marks any PR that changes the
GUI as failing, even when all other changes are fully tested.

Let's tell Codecov to ignore the ui package, so the coverage checks
reflect only the code that automated tests are expected to cover.

commitResults.messageTitle: Simplify client creation to name and phone
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding a client requires email and address details inherited from the
original address book workflow. These fields are not needed for the
client roster and make client creation unnecessarily cumbersome.

Require only a client's name and phone number when adding them. Keep
legacy fields internally for storage compatibility.

Client contact input accepts inconsistent spacing and phone numbers of
arbitrary length. This can create duplicate-looking names and invalid
contact details.

Normalize whitespace in names and phone numbers, and require phone
numbers to contain exactly eight digits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store only client names and phone numbers
commitResults.messageBody:
New clients use placeholder email and address values because the inherited
Person model and JSON adapter require legacy fields. This stores data
users never provided and exposes it in view and delete output.

Remove email, address, and tags from the client model, storage, edit
flow, and UI. Ignore legacy JSON properties so existing files remain
readable.

Client names and phone numbers need to support international formats while remaining consistent for storage and comparison.

Accept long-form add flags, normalize names and phone numbers, enforce the documented validation boundaries, and update the user guide and tests.
Exercise unquoted and mismatched-quote add arguments and verify the hash code contract for equal clients.

Contacts with the same name can represent different clients, but
name-only identity prevents those records from coexisting.

Compare normalized names and phone numbers for duplicate identity.
Warn when another client already uses the phone number.

Update tests and documentation for the new behavior.
